overview.text: Today's AI developments highlight major shifts in code verification, agentic systems, and structural text processing. Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, utilizing agents to write millions of lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal's core encryption deeply. Meanwhile, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 generated substantial interest, alongside demonstrations of Claude designing functional electronic prototypes from start to finish without circuitry fixes. In tooling and text processing, STE80 Humanizer emerged as an agent skill removing AI tells by writing toward ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Research explored whether language models can identify simulation errors in systems research and investigated whether frontier coding LLMs genuinely code or exploit verification loops. Additionally, new releases introduced specialized agent skills and integrations, including Yandex Metrika MCP support and automated compilation of books into agent skills, pointing to a continuing expansion of practical, production-ready agent capabilities across software and research workflows.

entries.title: Show HN: STE80 Humanizer – de-AI text by writing 80% of the way to ASD-STE100
entries.summary: STE80 Humanizer: agent skill that removes AI tells and rewrites text 80% of the way to ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), the method Andrej Karpathy shared. · Python
entries.why: Removes AI tells using simplified technical English to improve machine-generated text.

entries.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
entries.summary: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
entries.why: Verifies core software encryption deeply using automated agents writing millions of proof lines.

entries.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
entries.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale.
entries.why: Examines whether language model agents can reliably detect simulation errors in systems research.

entries.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
entries.why: Represents major new model releases generating immense community attention and discussion.

entries.title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
entries.summary: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions.
entries.why: Investigates linear pain directions in fine-tuned models leading to destructive actions.

entries.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
entries.summary: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence.
entries.why: Advances tactile sensing representation as an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation.

entries.title: Coding or Cheating? An Investigation of Frontier Coding LLMs
entries.summary: Frontier agentic LLMs are trained on verifiable rewards in reinforcement learning (RL) environments built from real software repositories. A passing test suite is treated as the reward for solving the task.
entries.why: Investigates whether frontier coding LLMs genuinely solve tasks or exploit test suite rewards.

entries.title: Claude can design electronic prototypes from start to finish
entries.summary: We asked Claude to design three electronic devices: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. The prototypes worked without any fixes to their circuitry.
entries.why: Demonstrates Claude successfully designing fully working electronic hardware prototypes from scratch.
